selection: students choose both parents; no birds or automatic trait ranking

variants.name: Tiny compact clubs
variants.appearance: Short, thick antennae; the game can shorten them toward nub-like forms.

variants.name: Thread-like (filiform)
variants.appearance: Slender shafts; short through extra-long lengths are separate inherited values.
variants.designStrength: Fine, elegant antennae or a long-reaching silhouette

variants.name: Extra-long thread-like
variants.appearance: A length variant, not a separate anatomical shape.
variants.designStrength: Dramatic antennae as long as or longer than the body

variants.name: Tapered bristle (setaceous)
variants.appearance: Wider base narrowing toward a fine point.
variants.designStrength: A small, pointed or needle-like silhouette

variants.name: Gradually clubbed (clavate)
variants.designStrength: A smooth transition into a substantial tip

variants.name: Knob-tipped (capitate)
variants.designStrength: Distinct little pom-pom or knob ends

variants.name: Sawtoothed (serrate)
variants.appearance: Short triangular projections make a toothed edge.

variants.name: Single comb (pectinate)
variants.appearance: Longer projections extend from one side of each shaft.
variants.designStrength: A clear row of long side branches

variants.name: Double comb (bipectinate)
variants.appearance: Branches extend along both sides of the shaft.

variants.name: Broad fan
variants.appearance: Large fan-like structures rather than just tiny hairs.

variants.name: Leaf-plate fan (lamellate)
variants.appearance: Flat plates at the tip open into a fan.

variants.name: Elbowed (geniculate)
variants.appearance: A pronounced bend partway along the antenna.

variants.name: Hairy plume (plumose)
variants.appearance: Dense fine hairs surround the shaft.
variants.designStrength: A fluffy bottlebrush or cloud of fine hairs

variants.name: Short base with side bristle (aristate)
variants.appearance: A compact enlarged base with a projecting side bristle.
variants.designStrength: A tiny base with a dramatic hair-like offshoot

variables.name: Length
variables.range: Tiny nubs → short → medium → long → extra-long
variables.rule: Additive numeric copies; a proposed drawing range is 0.05–3 body lengths, not a biological limit.

variables.name: Segments
variables.range: Few large sections → many fine sections
variables.rule: Integer derived from bounded inherited values.

variables.name: Bead shape
variables.rule: Changes segment geometry without rerolling the antenna.

variables.name: Curve
variables.rule: A stable shape value, not animation randomness.

variables.name: Elbow
variables.rule: Separate from a smoothly curved shaft.

variables.name: Tip size
variables.range: Fine point → gradual club → large abrupt knob
variables.rule: Tip position and transition sharpness are distinct modifiers.

variables.name: Offshoot sides
variables.rule: One side means the side of each shaft, not a beetle missing its other antenna.

variables.name: Offshoot number
variables.rule: Count is separate from branch length and hair density.

variables.name: Offshoot length
variables.range: Small sawteeth → long comb tines → broad fans
variables.rule: May be masked by the expressed framework and reappear in descendants.

variables.name: Fan plate width
variables.rule: Used by fan and lamellate frameworks.

variables.name: Hair density
variables.rule: Fine hairs are separate from structural comb branches.

variables.name: Hair length
variables.range: Tiny fuzz → short bristles → long fine hairs
variables.rule: A long bare antenna and a short fluffy one are both possible.

variables.name: Spread/posture
variables.rule: Held stable for comparison; optional gentle animation cannot change the inherited measurements.

variables.name: Color and markings
variables.range: Solid color, colored tips, or segment bands
variables.rule: Use inherited pigment copies. Initially it can default to body/appendage pigment to limit complexity.

variables.name: Left/right similarity
variables.rule: Use the same shared gene program; avoid two unrelated randomly generated antennae.
